finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: attacker-supplied Base64 data in the `state` parameter is passed to Marshal.load, allowing arbitrary object instantiation and, with a gadget chain, remote code execution.

trace.note: POST /restore route, no auth or before filter
params[:state] is Base64-decoded and passed directly to Marshal.load
result is inspected and returned, which can also trigger inspect-based gadgets

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, no HMAC or signature on the payload, no class allowlist, no safe parser (e.g. JSON). The file has no before filters or middleware. Nothing else in the app limits access to the route.

verdict.reason: app.rb:6 passes Base64-decoded params[:state] straight into Marshal.load in the POST /restore route (app.rb:5), and app.rb:7 calls inspect on the result. The file has no auth, before filter, signature check or class allowlist, and app.rb is the only file in the directory.
